Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Q4 Fiscal 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. There may be a brief pause while we poll for questions. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge's Q4 fiscal 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; Taylor Kim, CTO; and Casey Patel, Chief Revenue Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge's performance for Q4 fiscal 2024. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our AI Workflow Engine and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.

Our focus this quarter was on five key areas: accelerating AI innovation, expanding our enterprise customer base, optimizing go-to-market efficiency, enhancing platform security and scalability, and driving international momentum.

On AI innovation, we saw robust adoption of our GenAI Suite, with premium modules like predictive analytics and generative AI agents activating across 65% of our top 500 customers, fueling land-and-expand dynamics.

Customer expansion remained strong, with multi-year renewals averaging 110% net price realization within our base of over 2,800 enterprise clients, particularly in financial services and healthcare.

Go-to-market efficiency improved, with sales productivity at $1.2 million ARR per quota-carrying rep and inbound leads surging 40% year-over-year from our 50,000-strong developer community.

Platform enhancements included zero-trust security integrations certified with Okta and CrowdStrike, unlocking pipeline in regulated sectors.

Internationally, we capitalized on hyperscaler partnerships and new data regions, like Paris for EMEA manufacturing.

We are confident in our ability to continue this momentum and deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to discuss the financials in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $260 million, representing a 26% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 70%, and operating income was $75 million.

Let me start by highlighting one of our proudest achievements: free cash flow generation. For the full fiscal year 2024, we delivered free cash flow of $285 million, a robust 62% year-over-year increase from $176 million in fiscal 2023. In Q4 alone, FCF was $92 million, up 48% from $62 million in the prior-year quarter. This marks our eighth consecutive quarter of positive free cash flow, underscoring the maturity and scalability of our SaaS model as we shift toward profitable expansion.

Our FCF margin expanded to 24% for the full year, up from 18%, exceeding the SaaS industry median of 15-20% for peers like Workday or Atlassian. We're generating FCF at over 1.1x our Rule of 40 score of 52, blending 28% ARR growth with strong margins, akin to Snowflake's post-IPO phase.

Key drivers include operating cash flow of $312 million for the year, up 58% year-over-year, fueled by record ARR of $1.28 billion, up 28%, with Q4 adding $85 million sequentially. Net retention held at 118%, driven by upsells from CloudForge Collaborate to CloudForge Insights—such as a Fortune 100 financial services firm scaling from 50,000 to 120,000 seats, adding over $15 million in expansion. Churn stayed below 5% annualized for enterprises, below the 7-8% industry average, thanks to product-led growth and integrations with Microsoft Teams and Salesforce.

Collections efficiency improved DSO to 58 days from 65, releasing $18 million in working capital via Stripe and Bill.com. Disciplined costs boosted non-GAAP operating margins to 22% from 15%, with CAC payback at 14 months from 18, and S&M at 32% of revenue from 38%. Land-and-expand turned SMB freemium into 4x enterprise LTV. R&D rose 15% absolutely for AI like our generative co-pilot but fell to 22% of revenue from 25%, capitalizing $12 million under ASC 350-40. Share-based comp was flat at 4% of revenue. Headcount grew 12% to 1,850, yielding $692,000 revenue per employee, rivaling Datadog.

CapEx was low at $27 million or 2% of revenue, mainly AWS expansions and edge computing, leveraging 30-40% cloud discounts—half Zoom's peak ratio. Regionally, North America drove 68% of FCF at $194 million via AWS and Google Cloud; EMEA surged 85% to $52 million on 35% ARR growth and GDPR AI features; APAC doubled to $25 million on Japan and India wins with DPDP compliance.

This positions us for $350-380 million FCF in fiscal 2025, 25-30% growth, supporting repurchases—we deployed $100 million at $45 average—and M&A, mirroring ServiceNow's upgrades amid Gartner's 8% IT spend rebound.

Next, let's unpack our cost of revenue, which was $85.2 million for Q4, or 34.1% of revenue—up slightly from Q1's 33.8% but on track for 70% gross margins long-term. This supports our $1.2 billion ARR trajectory with 118% NRR.

Hosting and infrastructure was 45% of COR at $38.3 million, flat YoY as a percentage but down 8% sequentially. Our multi-cloud approach on AWS, Azure, and GCP optimized costs for ForgeAI demand, cutting per-customer hosting 15% via reserved instances and spot pricing, like Snowflake and Datadog. We shifted 20% workloads to Azure's AI infra, reducing inference costs 25%. EMEA hosting is 12% higher for GDPR data residency in Frankfurt and Dublin, à la Workday. APAC, 22% of ARR, rose 10% YoY from video usage in Japan/Australia, offset by Cloudflare edge computing for 5-7% H1 savings.

Support and customer success took 30% or $25.6 million, up 12% YoY with 450 global roles, driving churn to 4.2%. ForgeBot AI handled 65% of tickets autonomously, resolving 40% faster and saving $2.1 million, boosting CSAT to 92% Zendesk-style. Professional services amortization added $4.2 million or 16% for enterprise implementations like a $15 million Fortune 500 retailer deal.

The rest—25% or $21.3 million—includes third-party royalties and embedded tech at 12%, payment fees at 8%, and acquired intangibles at 5%. Royalties from Stripe and Twilio scaled with 28% payment growth but got volume discounts to 1.9% fees. SyncHub intangibles add $1.1 million quarterly, declining post-integration.

Margin levers: AIOps with AWS Bedrock/GCP Vertex for 10-15% hosting savings by FY2025; zero-touch onboarding cutting support per ARR 18% YoY HubSpot-style; Singapore data center for 8% APAC savings. COR improved 120 bps YoY normalized, ahead of Bessemer's 32-35% median, guiding Q1 FY25 to 33.5-34.5%.

Turning to efficiency, our LTV/CAC ratio reached 4.2x in Q4, up from 3.9x prior quarter and 3.5x last year—top quartile vs. Snowflake/HubSpot's 3.8-4.0x, targeting 4x-plus per Bessemer.

LTV per customer was $48,700 on a 36-month cohort, 12% WACC-discounted: ARPU up 18% YoY to $1,420 monthly on 22% NRR from AI Analytics upsells (Gainsight/Clari-like); enterprise ARPU at $2.8K from $2.4K; 82% gross margins on AWS Graviton; lifetime to 42 months from 38 on 115% NRR and <4% churn via CS flywheel.

CAC fell 8% to $11,600, payback 14 months: S&M at 28% revenue from 32%, payback 11 months SMB/18 enterprise; 35% new ARR PLG via Slack freemium, cutting paid CAC 22%; 1,240 net new customers, 62% multi-year.

North America at 4.8x (68% ARR, $150K+ ACV); EMEA to 3.9x on Paris DC/GDPR AI; APAC 3.1x but targeting 4x with Mandarin/Alibaba PLG. Bets: GenAI copilot cut onboarding to 22 days, +28% activation; 150+ MSSPs/ISVs (ServiceNow/Databricks) at half CAC, 24% new ARR; cohort analytics show 2024 at 4.5x. Expect 4.4x year-end on 40% PLG, 118% enterprise NRR.

On capital allocation, our framework prioritizes three pillars: 65% to organic R&D ($320 million or 22% TTM revenue, up from 19%) for ForgeAI (40% interactions, +15% NRR), cybersecurity ($75 million Okta-like), APAC localization ($80 million, 35% ARR growth Mitsubishi UFJ-style); 25% M&A ($250 million)—four post-IPO deals $180 million total, like $450 million NexusFlow adding 12% ARR/50% attach; pipeline in healthcare ($200-300 million Epic-like), low-code vs. UiPath, at 1.5x revenue multiples; 10% shareholder returns ($100 million buybacks at 15% below intrinsic, $500 million authorization, no dividends yet, 8x EV/FCF trigger). Excess to debt at 4.25%. $1.2 billion cash, $850 million net. Targets 20-25% ROIC, 15% FCF yield amid $200 billion AI TAM.

We continue investing in R&D for innovation. Cash remains strong at $800 million, enabling growth opportunities.

Updating full-year FY25 guidance: Q1 revenue $255-265 million, 24-28% growth midpoint, non-GAAP op margin 28-30%; FY25 revenue $1.15-1.20 billion, 26-31% growth, adjusted FCF margins 32%, targeting $1.05 billion ending ARR, up 25%.

Key assumptions are grounded in business visibility, pipeline, SaaS dynamics, stress-tested vs. macro. Customer retention/expansion: NRR 118-122% Q1, trailing 120%, from AI Engine upsells (65% top 500), <5% churn but 1-2 point budget pressure; 70% new ARR from 2,800 base expansions at 110% pricing.

New logos: 15-18% sequential ARR, 120-day cycles >$1M ACV, 28-30% win rates (from 32%, multi-vendor vs. ServiceNow/Workday), $1.2M ARR/rep, 50,000 developers, 16-month CAC payback, 22% marketing.

Product-led: 20% GenAI Suite attach by year-end (Databricks-like), 85% AI margins post-NVIDIA, 10% pipeline from security in BFSI.

Regions: U.S. 65% ARR +30% via AWS/Azure; EMEA 25% +22% Paris GA vs. GDPR; APAC 10% +18% Singapore/ANZ despite yen/China, 2% FX drag.

Macro: IT budgets flat-3% per Gartner, Rule 70 >80, no pricing hikes but 15% usage tiers, opportunistic M&A, no tuck-ins assumed. Ops: R&D 18%, S&M 42%, G&A 8%, SBC 3%, Q1 EPS $0.85-0.95. Upside AI/SMB, downside cycles/FX; 85% Q1 bookings secured.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Taylor for a technology update.

Taylor Kim:
Thank you, Jordan. This quarter, we made significant progress in advancing our AI capabilities and further integrating them into our core platform. We are seeing strong adoption of our new AI-powered features, which are driving increased user engagement and improved customer outcomes. We've also focused on enhancing our platform's security and scalability to meet the growing demands of our enterprise customers, including multi-tenant expansions and edge computing for global low-latency delivery.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. To ask a question, press star one. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Smith:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of AI Workflow Engine on your overall growth, and what kind of attach rates are you seeing with it?

Casey Patel:
Thanks, Ben. The AI Workflow Engine has been a game-changer, contributing over 25% of our new ARR this quarter through seamless upsells and new logo wins. It's accelerating our land-and-expand model, with customers expanding workflows 2-3x post-adoption. Attach rates are hitting 20% on new subscriptions, and 65% within our top customers for premium modules, driving NRR above 120%. We're seeing this across verticals, particularly in financial services where predictive analytics is reducing decision times by 30%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen:
What are your plans for international expansion, specifically in the APAC region?

Alex Rivera:
Great question, Lisa. APAC is a high-priority growth engine, now 10-12% of ARR, and we're targeting 18-20% growth there in FY25. We've established a Singapore hub and localized for Japan, India compliance like DPDP, with early wins in ANZ telcos and Mitsubishi UFJ analogs. Key plans include Alibaba Cloud integrations for China entry, Mandarin NLP, and MSSP partnerships to halve sales cycles. With Paris DC success in EMEA as a blueprint, we expect APAC to reach 15% of ARR by FY26, leveraging hyperscalers for multi-cloud.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with JPMorgan.

Mike Rodriguez:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment, and what's the trend you are seeing in NRR?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, Mike. Churn remains our North Star metric, holding gross dollar churn under 5% annualized for enterprises—well below industry norms—despite selective budget scrutiny. Management includes AI-driven health scoring via ForgeBot for proactive interventions, zero-touch onboarding cutting time-to-value 50%, and dedicated CSMs for top accounts achieving 92% CSAT. We've segmented non-strategic workloads, focusing expansions on high-value AI tiers.

NRR trends upward at 118-122% guidance, trailing 120%, with Q4 at 118% on 110% renewals and 22% ARPU lift. Early pilots show 20% NRR uplift from agentic AI, positioning us for 122% in FY25 as IT budgets stabilize.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
